answer: A mature reputational economy starves sybils via a trust maturation period. Each identity earns reputation only by continuous, signed participation across epochs, like a river depositing silt. New or cloned agents start at zero, unable to bid until an aging window closes, during which they sign honestly and hold a locked stake. An attacker spawning a hundred clones must lock a hundred stakes for weeks, and any whisper of misbehavior forfeits them. Reputation weights form a trellis only long-lived vines can climb: volume is cheap, influence expensive, so cloning becomes a sink.
